transcript:
Meeting: Request audit & telemetry controls walkthrough
Date/Time: 2026-01-15 14:00 UTC   Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO - Cascade Health), Ethan (Head of InfoSec), Rosa (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick live walkthrough of the Console controls for request storage, masked logging, retention toggles, and audit exports. Focus on compliance posture (SOC2/DPA), how redaction interacts with caching/kv cash, and what logs look like for auditors.

Topics: retention toggles, masked logging, request storage vs ephemeral, exportable audit logs, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, canary policies for toggles.

00:00 Sofia (Redwood AE): hi everyone, thanks for joining, today devon and i will run through the console and the API flags for request storage and telemetry, um we'll show how masking works and what the audit exports look like
00:18 Maya (CTO): thanks, yeah we're mainly here because legal and security asked for concrete examples — they want to see exactly what gets stored and how we can redact PHI before anything hits long term storage
00:29 Devon (Redwood SE): quick agenda: 1) a short API walkthrough for request-level toggles, 2) console demonstration of masked logging and retention windows, 3) how to run a compliance audit export, and 4) Q&A + next steps
00:45 Ethan (InfoSec): quick note — we need to know if logs can be split by tenant and whether audit trails include full request payloads or just hashes
00:58 Devon: good call; we'll show tenant-level views and the masking options. also we'll mention the KV cache nuance — sometimes inference runtimes keep a kv cache which can leak prefixes if not handled by prefix eviction, we surface the cache settings in the console
01:20 Rosa (Platform): are you showing KMS-integrations for keys? we require customer-managed keys for long-term storage encrypt at rest
01:31 Sofia: yes, we have KMS/HSM integrations; in hosted we can either bring-your-own-kms or use redwood-managed keys depending on the contract
01:45 Maya: and retention windows? legal wants a 30/90/365 breakdown with ability to delete on demand
01:55 Devon: Console -> Settings -> Data & Retention — you can set global defaults and override per-model or per-route. we'll demo a per-route toggle that keeps requests ephemeral (no request storage), and another route with 30 day retention and masked logs
02:10 [screen share starts, slight audio pop] Devon: okay i'm in the console, top nav, go to observe -> request storage... noticed the UI may show 'request store' in some older snapshots, we label it Request Storage now
02:33 Devon: here's a route config: Route A — 'transcription-service' set to ephemeral: true, maskedLogging: true, retentionDays: 0
02:48 Rosa: when you set maskedLogging, is the masking done client-side or server-side? can we supply our own regex rules?
02:56 Devon: server-side. we have built-in rules for common PHI (SSNs, emails, credit cards) and also a custom rule set which you can upload via the API as JSON. caveat: very custom extractions may require a short integration step
03:12 Maya: do masked logs still store hashes so we can correlate sessions for debugging? we need to be able to link traces without seeing raw PHI
03:22 Devon: yes we store one-way salted hashes for configured fields; the salt is customer-specific when using BYOK KMS, otherwise salted by the redwood-managed secret. note: hashing is reversible only with the salt — so audit exports will show hashes not raw values
03:40 Ethan: we need to know retention of those salts — key rotation policy?
03:45 Sofia: key rotation is supported; when rotated the old salts are kept for a configurable archival window to allow log correlation; if you request full key purges we can truncate archival salts but that breaks historical correlation, will document this in the SOC2 notes
04:05 Devon: jumping back — i'll show an example of a redaction rule upload... (typing) here's a small sample JSON, you can see field paths and regexes, and you can scope rules by route or by model
04:28 Maya: could that slow inferencing? concerned about per-request regex overhead at high throughput
04:36 Devon: good question — we do rule compilation and we run masks in a streaming stage before persistence, it's optimized and we have a profiling mode. for very high qps you can push masking to a pre-processor lambda in your infra or enable a fast-path mask with simple substring rules
04:55 Rosa: and how does this interact with caching — for instance if KV cache stores tokenized prefixes that contain PHI, can that end up in logs?
05:05 Devon: right, KV cache is kept in memory by the runtime; by default we do not persist the cache to disk, but there are dump/diagnostic options which are gated by admin roles. we recommend ephemeral routes for PHI-heavy workloads to avoid any diagnostic dumps being required. also we provide an auto-eviction policy that prevents sticky PHI prefixes from living longer than X tokens
05:32 Ethan: what about audit logs? we need immutable exports for compliance at least once a month, and they should include who toggled what and when
05:42 Devon: audit logs show who changed route configs: user, IP, timestamp, before/after diffs. exports come in NDJSON and we support push to S3 or direct download. retention of audit logs can be configured independently from request storage
06:05 Maya: curious about the API flags — can we toggle request storage at request time or only at route-level?
06:12 Devon: both. there's a request header you can set to override for that call: x-redwood-request-storage: ephemeral | store-masked | store-raw (store-raw is disabled unless your org-level policy allows it). we'll demo a curl afterwards
06:30 [short pause, typing] 06:44 Devon: demo — curl to create a route with retentionDays: 30 and maskedLogging true — (reads) curl -X POST api.redwood/v1/routes -d '{"name":"ehr-proxy","retentionDays":30, "maskedLogging":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
07:03 Maya: in the enclave/on-prem case — can we set the default to never store request payloads but allow temporary storage for debugging that auto-expires?
07:12 Sofia: yes — Private deployments have a mode called ephemeral-first where request-logging is off by default; you can enable timeboxed debugging sessions that self-destruct after the window
07:25 Rosa: will those debugging sessions create entries in the global audit trail? we need the fact that a debug session happened recorded, without storing payloads unless approved
07:33 Devon: yes event metadata is always recorded (session started, user, approver if needed) but payload persistence is controlled separately — approved debugging creates a sealed blob with limited TTL and only admins can access
07:50 Ethan: about exports — can we push encrypted audit exports to our S3 bucket using our own KMS key?
07:58 Devon: yes. we have a destination connector to S3 with SSE-KMS using your KMS key. files are encrypted in flight and at rest, and the connector rotates credentials automatically when you rotate keys in KMS
08:14 Maya: are there sample policies we can give legal for DPAs and data residency? we need language that says data in EU regions will not leave EU, etc
08:22 Sofia: we'll include our regionalization docs and a DPA template. note: for hosted, region pinning is supported per-account; for Private you control the network egress
08:35 [screen scroll, Devon demonstrating UI] 08:44 Devon: here's a sample audit export — it contains NDJSON lines with eventType, user, route, before/after, timestamp. sensitive request payloads appear as masked fields or hashes per your masking config
09:02 Maya: can you show an example where PII is redacted in transit but full text stored for debug? (they want to check role separation)
09:12 Devon: role separation is enforced — you can grant Debug-Viewer role which sees rich metadata and non-PII traces, Debug-Admin can unmask with an explicit approval flow that is logged. unmasking requires a second approver in our recommended compliance setup
09:30 Ethan: if Debug-Admin can unmask, how's that audited?
09:33 Devon: unmask events are recorded as high-sensitivity audit events with the who/why/approval chain and include a TTL after which unmasked data is re-masked in storage
09:45 Rosa: are there hooks for SIEM integration? we use Splunk and want alerts on config drift and unusual export activity
09:53 Devon: yes we push alerts and audit streams to common SIEMs via webhook or Kinesis, and you can set alert rules in the console. also we support OCI/CW logs depending on region
10:10 [15m mark roughly; conversation continues with scenarios and objections] 15:02 Maya: one of our main concerns is test data — we run a lot of synthetic tests that accidentally include real PHI in dev. is there a test-mode to block any request that matches sensitive patterns from ever leaving the VPC?
15:18 Devon: yep — the safety gate feature blocks outbound exports for flagged routes; you can set it to warn or block. for dev environments we recommend block-by-default and a small allowlist for specific integrations
15:35 Ethan: we also need to show to auditors that retention policies are enforced — is there a time series showing when records were deleted?
15:42 Devon: deletion events are recorded in the audit logs with a pseudo-delete proof: we store a tombstone hash of the deleted blob so you can prove deletion occurred without retaining the content
15:55 Rosa: is the tombstone hash compatible with our e-discovery requirements? we need to tie it back to an original request id for legal holds
16:03 Devon: you can preserve mapping keys for legal hold windows; when a legal hold is placed we disable deletion for the affected set and flag them in the audit index; that state is exportable for discovery
16:20 [glitch in transcription: "K V cash" appears instead of KV cache twice] 16:45 Maya: what about performance? implementing masking at high qps is a concern — can you give numbers or do we need a POC?
16:54 Devon: we can share internal benchmarks; typical mask microservice adds ~2-8ms p50 if using compiled rules. for worst-case regexes it can be higher. recommend a short POC with a replay of a representative sample, which we'll run with our optimize team
17:12 Sofia: i'll coordinate the POC run — devon will collect logs and show before/after cost delta using Redwood Optimize suggestions
17:25 Ethan: on the legal front, our counsel will want encryption-in-flight and key custody language spelled out — do you have standard contract addenda?
17:34 Sofia: yes, we'll include the DPA template and key custody appendix. we'll also include our SOC2 report extract and the list of sub processors
17:48 Rosa: one more technical — how do you handle function/tool-calling traces? sometimes inputs to tools are third-party and include PHI and we don't want those stored in a third-party tool integration
17:58 Devon: tool-call payloads are considered request content; by default they're subject to route masking rules. for external tool calls we support proxying through a VPC connector so you can route those calls via your network and avoid Redwood-managed third-party integration
18:15 Maya: can we set a per-customer policy that disables third-party connectors entirely?
18:21 Sofia: for Private deployments yes; for hosted we can restrict connectors at the org level and require explicit enablement after security review
18:35 [customer asks for live curl test] 18:44 Devon: ok live curl, i'll flip a retention toggle at the route level and then make a sample request with PII-ish content, then show what appears in the audit index
19:02 Devon: curl -X POST api.redwood/v1/routes/ehr-proxy/toggle -d '{"retention":"ephemeral","maskedLogging":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
19:22 [curl exec, brief pause] 19:31 Devon: now posting the sample request body (patient_name: "John Doe", ssn: "123-45-6789", notes: "patient has diabetes")
19:40 [console output] 19:44 Devon: audit event created: eventType: request.received, requestId: r-0a1b2c, route:ehr-proxy, masked:true
19:55 Maya: show us the stored object
20:01 Devon: here's the stored object: {patient_name: "<REDACTED>", ssn: "<REDACTED>", notes: "<REDACTED>", _hashes: {patient_name: "h:0x9f3a", ssn: "h:0x4b2d"}}
20:20 Ethan: looks good. can we search by the hash to find related sessions?
20:26 Devon: yes search by hash in the console and you get the associated request IDs — again, salt scoping is important for cross-org searches
20:40 [discussion about deletion proof and legal hold continues] 26:03 Rosa: we need a runbook for incident response — what steps do you provide if a misconfig or accidental retention occurs?
26:15 Devon: we have a documented IR flow: detection -> quarantine (auto-disable route) -> ephemeral snapshot export for triage -> either purge or escalate. we include timeline artifacts for the audit bundle which your team can ingest to your SIEM
26:40 Maya: can we test the runbook as part of the POC?
26:47 Sofia: yes that's part of the POC scope, we'll simulate a misconfig and walk through the remediation steps with your ops team
27:03 Ethan: minor nit — is there a way to prevent engineers from downloading raw exports unless they have a legal reason?
27:10 Devon: role gating + just-in-time approvals do that — downloads require an approver flow and are recorded as sensitive events. we also support temporary access tokens with TTL
27:25 [end-to-end policy and corporate policy discussion] 33:10 Maya: so to summarize: we want a POC that shows masked logging at scale, a replayed workload, audit exports to our S3 with our KMS, and an incident simulation. legal wants the DPA and SOC2 extracts.
33:26 Sofia: yep, we'll package that. next steps: we send docs, set up the POC timing, and devon will record the console walkthrough video for your team
33:40 Rosa: can you also include an example retention policy JSON we can drop into terraform? makes approvals faster
33:48 Devon: sure, i'll attach a sample terraform snippet and route config in the follow-up email
33:56 Maya: one more question on metrics — can we tie deletion events to billing events for cost transparency?
34:05 Devon: Optimize shows cost per-token and can break down cost impact of retention policies; deletion doesn't create a billing credit but you'll see reduced storage costs after retention window expires; we'll include a sample cost model for your expected volume
34:22 [wrap up and some small talk] 50:10 Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow up and schedule the POC planning meeting — any final questions?
50:22 Ethan: none for now; thanks for the clear demo
50:28 Maya: appreciate the thoroughness, look forward to the POC materials
50:35 Rosa: thanks, bye
50:38 Devon: thanks all, bye
